claims.sentence: NICE draft guidance proposes that two non-invasive diagnostic tests for endometriosis could be used in NHS primary care while more evidence on their accuracy is gathered.
The two tests are Endotest, which analyses a saliva sample, and EndoSure, which measures electrical signals in the gut.
NICE says the average wait for an endometriosis diagnosis is more than nine years.
NICE has published draft guidance proposing that two non-invasive diagnostic tests for endometriosis could be used in the NHS in primary care while more evidence on their accuracy is gathered.
Endotest analyses a saliva sample for tiny biological markers called microRNAs.
EndoSure detects endometriosis by measuring electrical signals in the gut.
NICE says the average wait for an endometriosis diagnosis is more than nine years.
A third test, DotEndo, which is a blood test, is not among the tests in the draft recommendations.
Because this is draft guidance, the recommendations may change after consultation.
